question:
Choose the idiom / phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

It's no use __worrying about the past mishaps__.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Crying over spilt milk"** means worrying about something that has already happened and cannot be changed. (बीती बातों पर पछताना)

 
 
• **Example: **There's no point in** crying over spilt milk**; we should focus on how to fix the problem instead.
 
 

Therefore, the correct idiom for the given phrase is **"Crying over spilt milk."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Spill the beans** (राज़ खोलना): To reveal secret information unintentionally or indiscreetly.

 
 
• **Example:** She accidentally **spilled the beans** about the surprise party.
 
 
 
• **Off on the wrong foot** (गलत शुरुआत करना): To make a bad start at something.
 
 
• **Example: **We got **off on the wrong foot **during our first meeting, but now we get along well.
 
 
 
• **Back to the grind** (फिर से काम पर लग जाना): Returning to one's usual work or routine, often after a break.
 
 
• **Example:** After a relaxing vacation, it's time to get **back to the grind.**
